correctness.rationale: The two atomic mean-field characteristics follow by substituting the measure into the published Vlasov velocity. For each topic the gap has a scalar uniformly positive contraction rate, so both gaps stay positive and converge exponentially; the two camp opinions have a common limit. The derivative of the normalized gap ratio has sign controlled by beta times the gap difference, yielding the sign of (q1-q2) and preserving gap order. An exact weighted-mean derivative integrates to the positive-quadrature identity for theta2-theta1; it proves necessity and sufficiency of all four zero-bending cases, without any numerical inference. Differentiation at beta=0 with uniform exponential bounds gives the explicit positive J(c) logarithmic coefficient. The packaged standard-library checker verifies the source-equation algebra in 81 rational parameter combinations and separately corroborates the strict example and small-beta limit. No finite computation is relied on to prove an infinite-time assertion.

value.rationale: An ordinary scalar compromise model preserves the segment between two initial camps. The published multidimensional theory proves coordinatewise containment only, leaving whether heterogeneous topic importance destroys the stronger and interpretable one-dimensional camp-to-camp interpolation unresolved. The theorem completely classifies the first nontrivial two-topic, two-camp setting under a natural affine positive influence kernel: exactly which degeneracies preserve the original segment, which direction the final consensus bends, and how the displacement first appears as topicwise distance sensitivity is introduced. The exact sharp boundary and universal positive integral yield structural information beyond routine convergence or a numerical counterexample.
